Standard/conventional SMC processing is limited to cutting rotors specifically for glass and compounding with thermoset polyesters and some epoxies. The multi-material, multi-format line developed in this project is flexible to enable custom conveying and uses an interchangeable rotor dedicated for specific material types. In this way, the asset will produce a wide range of SMC intermediates which will offer wide processing ability for applications in several IACMI projects. The overall tasks undertaken in this project included: Evaluation of the fiber feed mechanism, limiting tow conditions (fiber feed and spacing), and fiber feed distance for both glass and carbon fiber rovings to the rotary cutting section. In the rotary section, evaluated the effect of blade distance/spacing, blade angle, cot versus metal rollers (idle rolls) to name a few. The metal roller butts up against the rubber cot roller. The fiber passes between these two rollers. The cot roller provides the friction necessary to keep the fiber engaged as it passes through the roll pairs in the feed/cutting module. 1) This enabled optimization for both glass and carbon fiber feeds as well as basalt fibers. 2) The effect of textile grade carbon fiber sizing, such as epoxy and polyurethane on the cut quality was evaluated. Each fiber was expected to cut differently and learning on the material- cutter interactions would be gained. 3) Evaluated the servo motor conveying of the glass and textile grade carbon fibers feed to the line for uniformity of the chopping length, clean edges. We ran the servo motor controls at different speeds to evaluate the uniformity of the cut glass and carbon fibers. This ensured uniform quality SMC material downstream. 4) Evaluated the doctor box feed to the conveying elements for uniform resin film thickness. This film thickness has an influence on the consistent fiber volume fraction on the SMC produced therein. 5) Evaluated the compaction unit speed synchronization to the conveying module/section. Here we evaluated the 14 rolls and the spacing between the rolls, the effect of rolls compaction for differential heights to get different levels of compaction. Here we evaluated the fiber volume and SMC consistency as a combined function of the cutting steps, conveying, doctor box impregnation and compaction – all these factors are/were interrelated. 6) The future work will Evaluated different formulations, additives, constituents such as foam additives, different viscosity systems, resin chemistry and cure kinetics differences, mixing and agitation variations and resin film thickness to get a certain fiber weight fraction. The interrelations will be evaluated through statistical evaluation such as SAS JMP software. 4 7) The automation, PLC programming of various process steps and the safety of the carbon fiber processing is being continually updated.
